backlog.title: Close legacy evidence, traceability, payment routing, RED-GREEN, signed-review, and dirty-tree bypasses
acceptance: Schema v1 and trivial or unrelated verifier evidence cannot complete code changes.
Every acceptance ID maps to exact concrete invoked test references and the machine-derived execution manifest matches the command.
Every negative_paths entry has an exact negative_path_bindings record with an ID, acceptance IDs, and invoked refs.
Every final-tree verifier is replayed from its exact stored argv; a nonzero, missing, timed-out, or worktree-mutating command blocks completion.
Payment, billing, IAP, receipt, entitlement, subscription, and checkout work is always HARD/DEEP and requires contract, runtime, E2E, and signed review-2 evidence.
Fixes require the same verifier RED to GREEN chain; HARD fixes also require pre-mutation GREEN, mutation failure, and exact final GREEN with tree restoration.
Only OpenSSH Ed25519 review-2 signatures trusted by external DAINEXUS_REVIEW_ALLOWED_SIGNERS or ~/.dainexus/reviewers.allowed_signers can approve HARD work; review-1/self-authored JSON is UNVERIFIED.
Any staged, unstaged, tracked, or untracked nonignored source change invalidates prior evidence; secrets and private keys stay outside the workspace.

Verifier-owned evidence and volatile runtime memory, session, telemetry, cache, and review-handoff state cannot invalidate evidence merely by operating; arbitrary ignored project content remains fingerprinted.
An opaque platform-native Codex turn_id cannot shadow current evidence; selection is frozen once, while mapped-but-invalid selectors and non-correlated responses block.
Evidence and linked review reads are bounded regular-file operations that reject symlinks, path escape, and schema-v2 turn-to-filename mismatches.

status.summary: Three defects in the gate's own error handling, two of them mine from the day before. worktree_fingerprint had a 'refuse to guess' branch that raised, and an outer handler that caught the raise and returned GITERR:<hash of the error text> — a string shaped like a fingerprint, never matching anything, changing with the wording of the error. The other path raised outside that handler entirely and crashed the gate with a traceback instead of a verdict. Both are now one named failure, FingerprintUnavailable, which callers turn into a readable blocking check. Verified by forcing git to time out: no traceback, and the tree check reports UNVERIFIED with the reason. Second, a hard-signal turn was blocked unconditionally because this tree implements replay but not signed review-2 or chain validation. That made the repository unmaintainable by its own gate: hard_signal matches payment terms in the contents of changed files, and the file defining those terms is part of the gate, so any edit to it was permanently unverifiable. A gate that blocks indiscriminately gets switched off. Such a turn now completes only by declaring risk=hard and recording a hard-completion-unverified limitation, so it cannot pass by accident and the evidence carries a permanent statement that no independent review happened. Third, kernel/VERIFY.md and kernel/ESCALATE.md promised Ed25519 review-2 verification that no code here performs; they now state plainly what is enforced and what is not, because an unenforceable guarantee in the boot payload is worse than an honest absence. Also corrected a claim I made without measuring: replay does not slow the hook the way I reported. The real figures from the CI reports are unit 474s to 634s and gate 156s to 246s. Also: the gate could not validate itself during a commit. Every git call used a ten-second timeout, which is ample in a quiet shell and not while the pre-commit hook holds the index and replay fingerprints the worktree repeatedly — so the gate reported its own contention as a verification failure and the commit aborted at python-gate-tests after 464s, well inside its 1200s budget. Git calls now allow 45s, bounded at 180s and overridable, and the fingerprint retries four times with backoff before refusing. It still refuses when git genuinely never answers: verified at four attempts against a git that always times out. Finally, _find_evidence was ported from the reference. It had joined the payload's turn straight onto the verify directory with no validation, and with no turn given it took whatever file was newest — so a turn of '../../elsewhere' escaped the directory, a record whose internal turn disagreed with its filename was accepted, and a turn with no evidence of its own silently inherited one from days earlier. That last is what blocked every turn of this session with STALE and MISMATCH against a tree nobody was working in. Candidates now pass through read_evidence_json, which binds a v2 record's turn to its filename, and through the full validator chain. Gate suite 67 to 69 passing, 11 baselined, exactly matching. This was found only because local-ci now records a failing step's output: six earlier attempts reported nothing but an exit code. Then the measurement that explained the whole day: worktree_fingerprint hashed 25,911 ignored files totalling 346 MB on every call — all of node_modules, plus an 80 MB GitNexus index — and took about 40 seconds. The gate computed it up to five times per invocation. Hashing ignored content is deliberate so a change cannot be hidden in one, but node_modules is reproduced from the tracked lockfile and .gitnexus is derived from tracked source, so both are already covered transitively. Excluding them by name took the fingerprint to 3.9s, and threading the pre-replay value through cut five computations to three. The reference carries the same design and never felt it: that tree has no node_modules. With the gate no longer minutes slow, the suite's subprocess timeouts stopped expiring at random; they are now one named constant with headroom, and two consecutive runs give an identical 69 passing and 11 baselined. Amending the kernel then hit two of its own contract tests, which is the system working. A token budget caps VERIFY.md at 1000 tokens because it loads every session, and a policy test requires VERIFY.md to state the payment-review contract verbatim. Removing the promise outright failed the second; the honest resolution states both — what a verified HARD record must carry, and that this build does not check it — inside the budget at 996 tokens. Two more baselined unit tests now pass and were unpinned; both were the dead completion_checks import.
